thread:
maria: Heads up — several GPU pods in us-west-2 are showing repeated gRPC stream stalls during checkpoint uploads. Throughput drops to ~10% for 20–40s then recovers. Logs attached (snippet).

maria: ```
2024-04-08T12:03:11.234Z ERROR grpc: stream stalled, last ack=0, sent_bytes=524288
...
io.grpc.StatusRuntimeException: INTERNAL: stream reset
```

steve: I saw the same on the infra dashboard — TX retransmits + NIC errors on node-a-03 and node-b-11. RTTs spike, but p95 CPU on receiver increases too. Could be fragmentation/GSO mismatch with overlay.

raj: ran a quick tcpdump on pod iface — I see large segments being chopped and no ICMP frag-needed replies. path MTU probably being clamped by an intermediate device or ENI config.

infra-bot: [alert] high grpc retransmit rate on cluster/gpu-pool-usw2 (rule: grpc_stream_retries > 100 in 5m). Ticket created: INFRA-4782.

olivia: did iperf3 between two affected nodes, results weird.

olivia: ```
iperf3 -c 10.0.1.22 -l 16K -M 1500
SUM: sender 950 Mbits/sec
iperf3 -c 10.0.1.22 -l 16K -M 1450
SUM: sender 1.2 Gbits/sec
```

olivia: suggests larger MTU causes fragmentation / retransmits and lowers effective throughput.

steve: checked host NIC offloads: GSO enabled, GRO enabled on both ends. However the overlay (geneve) used by CNI adds ~80 bytes. If host MTU still 1500 but overlay expects 1420 we get silent drops.

steve: commands I ran: ```
# on node
ip link show dev eth0
ip link show dev gve0
ethtool -k eth0
sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing
```

steve: output: `gve0 mtu 1450`, `eth0 mtu 1500`, tcp_mtu_probing=0. So kernel will try to send 1500-1460 and fragmentation happens. No ICMP frag-needed seen due to cloud firewall dropping ICMP.

maria: that aligns with the gRPC stalls — high-volume streaming uses large segments and the receiver's stack gets overloaded with many fragments, causing reassembly bursts and stalls. RDMA paths were unaffected (we don't use RDMA on these nodes).

raj: mitigation options: 1) enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 temporarily so sender reduces size automatically; 2) force host MTU to match overlay (set eth0 to 1450) via daemonset; 3) disable GSO/GRO on host for affected NICs (reduces perf but avoids fragmentation).

olivia: quick test enabling tcp_mtu_probing=1 on node-b-11 reduced retransmits almost immediately.

olivia: ```
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1
# observed retransmits drop in ~10s
```

steve: tcp_mtu_probing is a good short-term hotfix. For long-term we should: update CNI mtu config to 1450 in the cluster/gpu-pool, bake ENI/user-data to set host mtu on boot, and add an e2e check in node provisioning that ensures eth0 mtu == cni_mtu + encap_overhead.

maria: rollout plan? we need minimal disruption — GPU jobs are sensitive.

raj: propose runbook: 1) set tcp_mtu_probing=1 cluster-wide for gpu nodes via daemonset (no pod restarts); 2) update node image / cloud-init to set host MTU to 1450 for new nodes; 3) schedule rolling reboot for older nodes after maintenance window; 4) update CNI config and run integration tests.

steve: also add a kernel bug/limit note — some ASICS drop ICMP, so relying on PMTU discovery in cloud is brittle. We should add a monitoring alert for host MTU != expected and for growing fragment/reassembly queues.

maria: agreed. raj — can you own the hotfix (daemonset + ticket INFRA-4782) and coordinate with SRE for the reboot window? i'll draft the CNI change PR.

raj: on it. I'll push the daemonset in the next 15m and monitor.

infra-bot: [deploy] DaemonSet "mtu-probing-enable" applied to 12/12 nodes in cluster/gpu-pool-usw2 by raj.

olivia: after daemonset, seeing stream success rate go from 82% -> 99% and latency p99 dropped. GPU training throughput recovered.

maria: nice. Please record the postmortem items: - fix CNI mtu default, - infra check on node MTU at provisioning, - update runbook for future MTU mismatch detection. Assigning to INFRA-4782.

steve: i'll add a Grafana panel for reassembly queue depth + ICMP frag-needed drops.

raj: closing this thread, will update ticket with timelines for image change and node reboot schedule. Thanks all :thumbsup:
